LESSON: TRADE AND FINANCE IN ISLAM

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Muamalat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.5: Trade and Finance in Islam
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Trade and Finance in Islam, part of Muamalat (Social Relations) in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why should Muslims observe the rules of borrowing and lending money?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the Islamic rules on borrowing and lending money,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. practise Islamic teachings on borrowing and lending money to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.),

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the role of consumer protection agencies to enhance integrity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the Islamic concept of borrowing and lending money as a means of safeguarding equity in the society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the Islamic rules on borrowing and lending money,

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. practise Islamic teachings on borrowing and lending money to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.),

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. describe the role of consumer protection agencies to enhance integrity,

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the Islamic concept of borrowing and lending money as a means of safeguarding equity in the society.

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the rules of borrowing and lending money in groups and make a class presentation,

2. visit an Islamic financial institution to learn more about borrowing and lending money and make notes,

3. listen to a resource person from consumer protection agencies to enlighten on consumer rights with regards to borrowing and lending money,

4. role play borrowing and lending money while observing the rules, learners with blindness can be given physical support as they role play.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the rules of borrowing and lending money in groups and make a class presentation,
2. visit an Islamic financial institution to learn more about borrowing and lending money and make notes,
3. listen to a resource person from consumer protection agencies to enlighten on consumer rights with regards to borrowing and lending money,
4. role play borrowing and lending money while observing the rules, learners with blindness can be given physical support as they role play.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Trade and Finance in Islam together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: the skill of seeking advice on information and support enhanced as learners visit an Islamic

financial institution to learn more about borrowing and lending money.

• Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening and speaking enhanced when learners discuss the rules

of borrowing and lending money in groups and make a class presentation.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of active listening and communication enhanced as learners

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. explain the Islamic rules on borrowing and lending money,
2. practise Islamic teachings on borrowing and lending money to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.),
3. describe the role of consumer protection agencies to enhance integrity,
4. appreciate the Islamic concept of borrowing and lending money as a means of safeguarding equity in the society.

Remember the key question: Why should Muslims observe the rules of borrowing and lending money?
